identity.title: Isotopic Ratios of Carbon and Oxygen in Titan’s CO using ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: Interferometric observations of Titan (obtained from the ALMA Science Archive and summarized in Table 2) were taken on multiple dates in 2012 and 2014.

evidence.quote: Titan’s diameter ranged from 0.67$^{\prime\prime}$ to 0.78$^{\prime\prime}$ on the sky throughout the observation dates.

question.value: What are the CO abundance and the 12C/13C, 16O/18O and 16O/17O isotopic ratios in Titan's atmosphere, derived from ALMA CO isotopologue lines?

evidence.quote: Molecular abundances and the vertical atmospheric temperature profile were derived by modeling the observed emission line profiles using NEMESIS, a line-by-line radiative transfer code.
Data from ALMA Bands 3, 6, 7, and 9 were used for this study.
Data sets from 2012 were a part of ALMA Early Science Cycle 0 observations, when the full array was not yet completed.

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: Archival data, often Titan flux calibration observations

evidence.quote: ALMA often uses Titan to calibrate the absolute flux scale for the science target, resulting in numerous short observations of Titan spanning the lifetime of ALMA.

what.value: Initial temperature profile from Cassini CIRS and Huygens HASI

evidence.quote: We adopted an initial atmospheric temperature profile derived from a combination of Cassini CIRS and Huygens Atmospheric Structure Instrument (HASI) measurements

what.value: Abundances of nitrogen and methane isotopes and aerosols

evidence.quote: Abundances of nitrogen and methane isotopes and aerosols were adopted from Teanby et al. (2013)
line parameters were extracted from the HITRAN 2012 database

what.value: Gas vertical profiles for N2, CH4, H2

evidence.quote: Gas vertical profiles for these molecules were based on (cite: niemann10).

what.value: Terrestrial isotopic ratios 89.3, 498.8, 2680.6 used as a priori

evidence.quote: we assumed terrestrial isotopic ratios of 89.3 for $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C, 498.8 for $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O, and 2680.6 for $^{16}$O/$^{17}$O

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 flux model for Titan used for the flux scale

evidence.quote: The initial flux scale was established by matching the continuum level from a relatively line free region in the spectrum to that of the Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 flux model for Titan

pipeline_or_manual.value: Revised JAO calibration scripts, with emission lines unflagged and updated Titan flux model

evidence.quote: The data were flagged and calibrated using revised versions of the calibration scripts provided by the Joint ALMA Observatory.
using version 4.3.1 of the Common Astronomy Software Applications package (CASA)

flux_calibrator.value: Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 Titan model; bandpass with bright quasars (e.g., 3C279)

evidence.quote: Bright quasars (e.g., 3C279) were used for bandpass calibration.
which is expected to be accurate to within 15%.

self_calibration.value: Phase self-calibration possible using Titan's continuum

evidence.quote: Self-calibration of the phases was possible due to Titan’s strong and compact continuum emission.
Image deconvolution was performed using the Högbom clean algorithm with natural visibility weighting and a threshold flux level of twice the expected RMS noise.
Image deconvolution was performed using the Högbom clean algorithm with natural visibility weighting and a threshold flux level of twice the expected RMS noise.

array_combination.value: C18O and C17O data combined per transition with fixplanets and cvel

evidence.quote: Measurements of C$^{18}$O and C$^{17}$O were combined for each transition using the CASA *fixplanets* and *cvel* tasks
Data reduction used a similar method to (cite: cordiner15) using version 4.3.1
In a similar manner to (cite: cordiner15), individual spectra were modeled using the NEMESIS line-by-line radiative transfer code
fluxes were converted to spectral radiance units (W/cm$^{2}$/sr/cm$^{-1}$) following the procedure outlined in (cite: teanby13).
results for all five emission lines were combined using the technique provided in (cite: nixon08a) Section 4.

method.value: Revised JAO scripts, phase self-cal, Högbom clean with natural weighting in CASA, Titan rest-frame correction

evidence.quote: spectral coordinates were corrected into Titan’s rest frame using JPL Horizons On-Line Ephemeris System
a threshold flux level of twice the expected RMS noise

analysis_steps.goal: Extract disc-averaged spectra and convert to radiance

method.value: Integrate over Titan disc plus atmosphere to 850 km plus 3 sigma_PSF; convert Jy to radiance

evidence.quote: We obtained spectra by integrating over a region of the ALMA data cube that includes the flux from Titan’s solid disc and atmosphere out to 850 km plus 3$\sigma$$_{PSF}$

validation.value: Spectra rescaled to NEMESIS continuum, differing ~10% from Horizons flux model

evidence.quote: which typically differed from the Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 flux model by about 10%.

analysis_steps.goal: Retrieve CO abundance and temperature profile

method.value: Simultaneous retrieval of constant CO VMR and temperature profile with a priori 50 ppm; limb-brightening via disc-averaged reference spectra

evidence.quote: We began with an a priori mixing ratio of 50 ppm and simultaneously retrieved a constant vertical abundance and temperature profile.

key_parameters.value: 24 to 27 field-of-view averaging points out to 3425 km radius

evidence.quote: The number of averaging points for this study ranged from 24 to 27

assumptions.value: CO mixing ratio constant with altitude up to 850 km

evidence.quote: we modeled the CO emission lines under the assumption that the mixing ratio remains constant with altitude up to 850 km

fitting.value: Iterative chi^2 minimization with a priori regularization; 2% line intensity systematic added

evidence.quote: NEMESIS uses an iterative $\chi^2$ minimization technique that relies on both the quality of the fit to the data and the level of deviation from the a priori setup.

validation.value: Correlation coefficients; fixed CO 40-60 ppm test with temperature-only retrieval

evidence.quote: We also tested the uniqueness of fit by holding the CO gas abundance at constant values between 40 and 60 ppm

analysis_steps.goal: Retrieve isotopologue abundances and isotopic ratios

method.value: Fixed nearest-in-time CO-retrieved temperature profile; a priori terrestrial ratios; fit each line and combine

evidence.quote: the retrieved temperature profile which was closest in time to that observation was used as the fixed temperature profile
we assumed terrestrial isotopic ratios of 89.3 for $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C, 498.8 for $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O, and 2680.6 for $^{16}$O/$^{17}$O
Best-fitting models of CO isotopologues were found using the same modeling procedures as CO (aside from the fixed temperature profile)

validation.value: C18O 3-2 and 2-1 abundances consistent within errors

evidence.quote: The mixing ratios for C$^{18}$O, derived independently from the J = 3–2 and J = 2–1 transitions, are consistent within the observational errors.
using version 4.3.1 of the Common Astronomy Software Applications package (CASA)
individual spectra were modeled using the NEMESIS line-by-line radiative transfer code
The Splatalogue database for astronomical spectroscopy was used to assign rest frequencies to the observed emission lines
spectral coordinates were corrected into Titan’s rest frame using JPL Horizons On-Line Ephemeris System
The abundance of CO was determined to be 49.6 ${\pm}$ 1.8 ppm

results_numeric.value: 8 K above 500 km; 4 K at 200 km

evidence.quote: Errors for the globally averaged retrieved temperature profile are of the order of 8 K at the top of the atmosphere (above 500 km) and 4 K at 200 km.

findings_qualitative.value: First spectroscopic detection of 17O in the outer solar system via C17O at >8 sigma

evidence.quote: We present the first spectroscopic detection of $^{17}$O in the outer solar system with C$^{17}$O detected at \>8$\sigma$ confidence.

claims.hypothesis: Titan's CO isotopic ratios deviate from terrestrial values
claims.experiment: NEMESIS retrieval of ALMA CO isotopologue lines
claims.finding: No significant deviation from terrestrial ratios

evidence.quote: Our results are in good agreement with previous studies and suggest no significant deviations from standard terrestrial isotopic ratios.

claims.hypothesis: CO is uniformly mixed in Titan's atmosphere
claims.experiment: Fit lines probing 140-550 km with a constant VMR
claims.result: Consistent abundances across transitions; CO 49.6±1.8 ppm

evidence.quote: Thus, the assumption of a constant CO abundance with altitude appears to be validated.

why_this_data.value: Archival Titan flux-calibration observations give many CO lines; dates chosen close in time to limit seasonal effects

evidence.quote: We selected observation dates within a short period of time to minimize possible effects of seasonal variations in Titan’s thermal structure.

limitations_admitted.value: Unquantified systematic errors (disc-averaged temperature, Voigt profile, line-broadening coefficients)

evidence.quote: Additional systematic errors that have not been quantified in the final error estimate could exist.
